title: The subgroup generated by a face is saturated
statement: Let $Q$ be a commutative monoid, written additively, which is integral (its canonical map to its group completion $Q^{\rm gp}$ [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] is injective) and saturated ($ng\in Q$ with $g\in Q^{\rm gp}$ and $n>0$ implies $g\in Q$), and let $F\subseteq Q$ be a face, meaning a submonoid such that $a+b\in F$ with $a,b\in Q$ implies $a,b\in F$. Then $F^{\rm gp}$ is a saturated subgroup of $Q^{\rm gp}$; equivalently, $Q^{\rm gp}/F^{\rm gp}$ is torsion-free.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.1.1--3.1.2, printed pp. 98--99; the face subgroup and torsion-free sharp characteristic used in the localization discussion.

mathlib_searches.query: For an integral saturated commutative monoid and a face, the subgroup generated by the face is saturated in the group completion
mathlib_searches.results: AddSubgroup.saturated_iff_zsmul and AddSubgroup.saturated_iff_nsmul; no face-specific theorem.

mathlib_searches.query: A saturated submonoid face generates a pure subgroup of the group completion
